question_text: A 52-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider with shortness of breath. She reports a 3-month history of difficulty breathing with exertion that has progressed to affect her at rest. She swims 45 minutes every day but has had trouble swimming recently due to her breathing difficulties. Her past medical history is notable for well-controlled mild intermittent asthma and generalized anxiety disorder. She has a 15 pack-year smoking history but quit 15 years ago. She does not drink alcohol. Her mother died at the age of 60 from heart failure and was a lifetime non-smoker. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, pulse is 85/min, and respirations are 22/min. Her BMI is 23 kg/m^2. On exam, she has slightly increased work of breathing. Cardiac auscultation reveals a normal S1 and loud P2. An echocardiogram is performed demonstrating right ventricular hypertrophy. Her pulmonary artery pressure is 24 mmHg at rest and 40 mmHg with exercise. This patient’s condition is associated with a mutation in a gene that does which of the following?
